papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal childhood brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations that create a dysregulated epigenetic landscape and extensive intratumoral heterogeneity. It discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, combined with computational modeling, could help uncover the mechanisms of treatment resistance that remain poorly understood.

papers.title: Intra-Abdominal Sporadic Desmoid Tumors with Canonical CTNNB1 and Uncommon Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway Somatic Mutations-A Clinicopathologic and Genetic Study of Five Cases.
papers.abstract: Desmoid tumors (DTs) may be sporadic or associated with familial polyposis syndromes, including familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and its variant, Gardner syndrome (GS). DTs are pathogenetically linked to activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. In sporadic DT, CTNNB1 is most frequently implicated, with exon 3 somatic mutations (T41A, S45F and S45P) being the most commonly reported. APC is implicated in FAP/GS-associated DTs and occasionally in sporadic DT, most often through alterations involving the exon 15 mutation cluster region. In this study of five sporadic intra-abdominal
papers.summary: This case series characterizes five sporadic intra-abdominal desmoid tumors, identifying canonical CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations alongside uncommon somatic alterations in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. The findings expand the known mutational spectrum beyond the typical T41A, S45F, and S45P hotspots, highlighting genetic heterogeneity in sporadic desmoid tumors. The work is primarily descriptive and limited by its small sample size.

papers.title: DUET-seq: An Open-Source Droplet Platform for High-Fidelity Joint Chromatin and Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Temporal Regulatory Decoupling in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: Joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell enables direct linkage of regulatory elements to transcriptional output, but existing approaches remain limited by low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high costs. Here we present DUET-seq, an open-source droplet microfluidic platform for joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus. DUET-seq combines programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads with one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to physically co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments, completin
papers.summary: DUET-seq is an open-source droplet microfluidic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus, using programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads and one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments. The platform achieves high co-capture sensitivity without proprietary components, and its application reveals temporal decoupling between regulatory element accessibility and transcriptional output in single cells.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, increasing tumor susceptibility to immune attack. The authors frame generative bioorganic design approaches as a route to next-generation BET-ICI combination agents.

papers.title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Microbiome Metabolites That Inhibit HDAC.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a family of key epigenetic regulator implicated in inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Microbiome metabolites can modulate host histone acetylation, yet systematic identification of metabolites that target HDAC remains limited. Here we present a computationally driven discovery pipeline that combines training data composition optimization with experimental validation to prioritize microbiome-derived HDAC inhibitors. Starting from a large, public HDAC3 screening data set (314,129 compounds; 485 actives), we developed an automated iterative sampling strategy that
papers.summary: The authors built a machine-learning pipeline to screen microbiome-derived metabolites for HDAC inhibition, starting from a large public HDAC3 dataset of over 314,000 compounds. They used an iterative sampling strategy to optimize training data composition and then experimentally validated prioritized candidates. This provides a computational framework for discovering microbiome metabolites that may influence host epigenetics.

papers.title: Allele-Specific MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci in a Hispanic/Latino Population: An Integrative GWAS, All of Us, and Epigenomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) disproportionately affects Hispanic individuals, who remain underrepresented in genomic discovery and lack ancestry-matched functional resources. Many CRC risk variants are non-coding, and those in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) can alter microRNA (miRNA) binding sites and reprogram post-transcriptional gene regulation. Here, we identify allele-specific miRNA-binding variants at CRC risk loci within the Hispanic population using a discovery pipeline anchored to Hispanic-relevant resources. CRC-associated 3' UTR variants were compiled from the GWAS Catalog, further ve
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS data with the All of Us cohort and epigenomic resources to identify allele-specific microRNA-binding variants at colorectal cancer risk loci in Hispanic/Latino populations. The work addresses the underrepresentation of this group in genomic research by uncovering non-coding regulatory variants that may alter miRNA binding and contribute to CRC risk. It provides an ancestry-matched functional framework for interpreting CRC-associated 3' UTR variants.

papers.title: SMORE: joint dimension reduction and cell population discovery on single-cell methylome data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling technology captures novel epigenetic data modality but are challenging to analyze because of their heterogeneity, high dimensionality, and ultra-sparsity. Here we present SMORE (Single-cell MethylOme Reduction and Embedding), a computational method for joint dimensionality reduction and cell population discovery dedicated to single cell DNA methylation data. SMORE operates on a Bayesian framework that converts methylation proportions into ordered methylation states and jointly infers a low-dimensional representation, cell populations and their number. By u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMORE is a new computational method for analyzing single-cell DNA methylation data, which is extremely sparse and high-dimensional. It uses a Bayesian framework to convert methylation proportions into ordered states and simultaneously performs dimensionality reduction and discovers cell populations (including their number) without needing to specify the number of clusters in advance. This addresses a key analysis bottleneck for the emerging single-cell methylome modality.

papers.title: The reference shapes the signal: chrX genotype summaries and classifier sex disparity between GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 callsets.
papers.abstract: Laboratories that move from GRCh38 to T2T-CHM13 take on a new callset as well as a new assembly. I asked whether the move changes sex-chromosome genotype summaries, and whether it changes how well classifiers trained on those summaries serve males and females. I compared the published 1000 Genomes GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 callsets for 3,202 people. The two callsets come from different alignment, calling, phasing and filtering workflows, so every difference below belongs to the reference and its pipeline together. In women, the fraction of non-reference chrX genotypes that were heterozygous was 0.6
papers.summary: This study compares chrX genotype summaries between the GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 1000 Genomes callsets for 3,202 individuals, finding that the reference assembly and its associated pipeline jointly alter sex-chromosome genotype summaries. These differences in turn affect how well classifiers trained on those summaries perform for males versus females, revealing a sex disparity tied to reference choice.

papers.title: DNAharvester: A Nextflow Pipeline for Analysing Highly Degraded DNA from Ancient and Historical Specimens.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences.
papers.summary: DNAharvester is a Nextflow pipeline designed to process highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens, addressing challenges like short fragments, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and contamination. It aims to reduce spurious mapping and reference bias, improving the reliability of downstream population genetic analyses for large-scale aDNA studies.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review compares targeted (amplicon- and probe-based) and untargeted sequencing strategies for wastewater virome surveillance, highlighting that targeted methods offer sensitive detection of known viruses but cannot identify novel pathogens. It also discusses bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater sequencing, providing guidance for moving beyond simple detection toward detailed pathogen characterization in population-level monitoring.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validat
papers.summary: This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond standard mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies. It finds that direct plasma evidence is strongest for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies remain retrospective and internally validated, limiting clinical translation. The authors outline current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions for these epigenomic and fragment-level approaches.

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network.
papers.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of human biology, yet the detection of somatic mutations remains challenging. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network conducted large-scale benchmarking experiments involving cell lines and donor tissues to evaluate sequencing technologies, experimental approaches, and computational methods for detecting different types of somatic mutations, generating community resources with >1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read data for nine analyzed samples. We determined effective strategies for utilizing short- a
papers.summary: The SMaHT Network benchmarked sequencing technologies, experimental protocols, and computational pipelines for detecting somatic mutations across cell lines and donor tissues, generating deep short-read (>1,000×) and long-read (100-400×) datasets for nine samples. The study identifies effective strategies for combining short- and long-read data to detect different classes of somatic mutations, and releases community resources to guide future mosaicism studies.

papers.title: Fast3VmrMLM enables statistically powerful and computationally efficient large-scale marker-pair epistasis GWAS in sizable populations.
papers.abstract: Identifying marker-pair epistasis in genome-wide association studies remains challenging due to computational burden and statistically underpowered. Hence, we developed a big-data algorithm, Fast3VmrMLM, that integrates a genome-wide pairwise scanning plus machine-learning framework with seven big-data techniques. Fast3VmrMLM considers all possible genetic effects while controlling for all polygenic backgrounds, substantially improving power of identifying epistasis. To broaden its utility, we extended three modules: Fast3VmrMLM-Hap for haplotype-by-haplotype interactions, Fast3VmrMLM-NCII for
papers.summary: Fast3VmrMLM is a new big-data algorithm that detects marker-pair epistasis in genome-wide association studies by combining genome-wide pairwise scanning with machine learning and seven computational techniques. It accounts for all possible genetic effects while controlling for polygenic background, substantially improving statistical power and computational efficiency for large populations. Extensions include modules for haplotype-by-haplotype interactions and non-additive/non-linear effects.

papers.title: Ryder: Epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions.
papers.abstract: Sequencing-based epigenomic profiling methods are powerful but suffer from technical variability that complicates cross-sample comparisons and can obscure true biological signals. While existing normalization methods using spike-in controls or computational approaches have been proposed, they often rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions or require additional data types.
papers.summary: Ryder introduces a two-tier normalization model for sequencing-based epigenomic data that uses internal reference regions to correct technical variability without requiring spike-in controls or additional data types. This approach aims to improve cross-sample comparability and preserve true biological signals across diverse experimental conditions.

papers.title: Integration of Collaborative Cross and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel studies does not significantly improve genome wide association study results.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies rely on maximizing cohort size and minimizing environmental noise to increase their efficacy. Model organism Genetic Reference Populations offer significantly reduced environmental noise and deep phenotyping, yet rarely are multiple populations merged together. We evaluated whether combining the Collaborative Cross (CC) and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel (HMDP), two well-studied murine Genetic Reference Populations would improve GWAS outcomes. Utilizing two prior studies by our group that had performed the same study for heart failure in each cohort, we examined e
papers.summary: The authors tested whether merging two mouse genetic reference populations, the Collaborative Cross and the Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel, improves genome-wide association study power for heart failure traits. Despite combining cohorts, the integrated analysis did not yield significantly better GWAS results than analyzing each population separately. This suggests that simply pooling genetically distinct reference populations may not be an effective strategy for boosting association signal.

papers.title: Interpretable neural networks prioritize cancer driver genes from genome-wide dependency landscapes.
papers.abstract: Identifying cancer driver genes and their therapeutic impact remains a core challenge in computational cancer biology. We introduce xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that connect cancer mutations with genome-wide DepMap gene dependencies, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised pathway-guided model that evaluates whether a gene's mutation status is encoded in the genome-wide dependency landscape; we interpret model fitness as a driver potential score, which quantifies the strength of this mutation-dependency signal and prioriti
papers.summary: The authors present xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that link cancer mutations to genome-wide DepMap gene dependency data, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised, pathway-guided model that scores how strongly a gene's mutation status is reflected in the dependency landscape, yielding a 'driver potential' score to prioritize candidate cancer driver genes. The approach aims to improve identification of driver genes and their therapeutic relevance by leveraging functional dependency data rather than mutation frequency alone.

papers.title: FAMUS: A Few-Shot Learning Framework for Large-Scale Protein Annotation.
papers.abstract: Gene function prediction is pivotal in genomic and metagenomic data analysis. Current annotation tools typically rely on the most similar sequence from the query database and struggle to robustly set meaningful hit thresholds, causing a major challenge for reliable annotation.
papers.summary: FAMUS introduces a few-shot learning framework for large-scale protein function annotation that moves beyond the standard approach of relying on the single most similar database hit with fixed thresholds. By learning from a small number of labeled examples, the method aims to make gene function prediction more robust and reliable, particularly for genomic and metagenomic analyses where threshold selection is a persistent problem.

papers.title: Prioritization of candidate genomic regions for milking speed in Holstein cattle using international evaluations.
papers.abstract: Milking speed (MSPD) is an economically important trait in dairy cattle affecting labor efficiency, animal welfare and milking parlor productivity. This complex quantitative trait has been investigated to characterize its genetic basis and support genomic selection. Previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have reported genomic regions potentially related to MSPD; however, results vary considerably among studies and often provide limited functional interpretation. This study aimed to prioritize candidate genomic regions for MSPD based on the ranking of estimated SNP effects from the Int
papers.summary: This study integrates international genetic evaluations to prioritize genomic regions associated with milking speed in Holstein cattle, a complex trait affecting labor efficiency and animal welfare. By ranking estimated SNP effects across populations, the authors identify candidate regions that are more consistent than those from individual GWAS, providing a more robust basis for genomic selection.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily model
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of AI in mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics across three generations: classical chemometrics/machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with LLMs currently playing only peripheral roles. It argues that despite the metabolome and lipidome being closest to drug action, these omics layers have lagged in AI adoption due to their downstream position, lack of a closed molecular reference, and absence of standardized, model-ready data.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including MMSE, MoCA, ADAS11
papers.summary: HINN is a deep learning framework that uses biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships and predict cognitive assessment scores from blood-derived multi-omics data. It aims to improve interpretability and leverage prior biological knowledge for biomarker prioritization in cognitive decline.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens.
papers.abstract: The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune
papers.summary: This review discusses how genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of ESKAPE pathogens can be combined with AI and multi-omics data to predict antibiotic resistance traits. GEMs simulate cellular metabolism across many conditions, generating large datasets that machine learning can mine to reveal how pathogens adapt to hosts and evade immunity. The authors argue this integration can accelerate discovery of resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: Beyond molecular snapshots: Regulatory trajectories in dynamic epigenetic regulation.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation is commonly interpreted through molecular markers measured at discrete timepoints. While such approaches have generated important biological insights, they primarily provide static representations of regulatory states and may therefore capture only a limited component of dynamic biological processes. Emerging evidence from chromatin biology, transcriptional regulation and genome organisation suggests that biological regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers. This article presents a biological hypothesis and conceptual f
papers.summary: This conceptual paper argues that epigenetic regulation is fundamentally dynamic and cannot be fully understood through static molecular snapshots taken at discrete timepoints. The authors propose a hypothesis framing regulation as continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers, including chromatin, transcription, and genome organization, and call for trajectory-based rather than snapshot-based interpretations.

papers.title: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has been shown to improve diagnosis beyond standard-of-care genetic tests and guide precision treatment for childhood cancer. While WGS is now offered for children with suspected cancer in England, clinical workflows typically return results after several weeks whereas clinical decisions are often required within days. Here we evaluate feasibility and efficacy of a rapid WGS (rWGS) research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics to deliver clinical genomic findings (NCT07201038, Active, not recruiting). In 54 children with suspected or confirmed malignancy, rWGS
papers.summary: This study evaluates a rapid whole-genome sequencing (rWGS) workflow with streamlined bioinformatics for children with suspected or confirmed cancer, aiming to return clinical genomic findings within days rather than weeks. In 54 pediatric patients, the approach was assessed for feasibility and its ability to improve diagnosis and guide precision treatment compared to standard genetic testing. The work demonstrates that rWGS can deliver actionable results fast enough to inform time-sensitive clinical decisions in pediatric oncology.

papers.title: Protocol for detecting germline copy number variants from whole-exome sequencing using agent-assisted Snakemake workflows.
papers.abstract: Germline copy number variants (gCNVs) are vital for diagnosing rare monogenic disorders. Here, we present a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake protocol for detecting, annotating, and visualizing gCNVs from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. We describe steps for constructing baseline models, executing CNV calling, annotating variant pathogenicity using public datasets, and rendering interactive visual reports. This automated workflow simplifies routine management and ensures cross-platform reproducibility through a unified interface.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake workflow for detecting, annotating, and visualizing germline copy number variants from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. It covers baseline model construction, CNV calling, pathogenicity annotation using public datasets, and interactive visual reporting, with the goal of improving reproducibility and simplifying routine management across platforms.

papers.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Phenotyping for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Algorithm Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
papers.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common psychiatric disorder, with two-thirds of affected individuals reporting severe impairment. Despite its substantial burden and moderate heritability, the etiology of OCD remains poorly understood, and treatments are often suboptimal. Although recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified some risk loci, much of the genetic architecture of OCD remains undiscovered, underscoring the need for scalable approaches to identify large, well-defined patient cohorts.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates an electronic health record-based phenotyping algorithm to identify patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder across multiple medical centers. The approach aims to enable scalable creation of large, well-defined OCD cohorts for genetic and clinical research, addressing the need for better-powered studies of this moderately heritable psychiatric disorder.

papers.title: Microbial community composition on polytetrafluoroethylene tape retrieved from implant screw channels: A cross-sectional high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing study.
papers.abstract: To identify the types of microorganisms colonizing the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape used for sealing the central screw channel in implant prostheses and to evaluate their association with the duration of prosthetic functional loading.
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbial communities colonizing PTFE tape used to seal the central screw channel in dental implant prostheses. The authors examined how community composition relates to the duration of prosthetic functional loading. The work provides a descriptive profile of the oral microbiome on this specific implant surface.

papers.title: Clinical Epigenomics in Rare Diseases: Interpreting DNA Methylation Episignatures.
papers.abstract: Epigenomic testing complements sequence-based analysis by detecting downstream changes in epigenomic state associated with genetic variation. Genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures are reproducible molecular phenotypes that can serve as biomarkers of specific Mendelian disorders, particularly those involving chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulatory pathways.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures—reproducible patterns of methylation that act as molecular fingerprints—can be used as clinical biomarkers for rare Mendelian diseases, especially those caused by mutations in chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulators. It argues that epigenomic testing complements standard DNA sequencing by capturing downstream functional consequences of genetic variants, aiding diagnosis when sequence alone is inconclusive.

papers.title: Analytical and clinical validation of the EdenDx methylation assay as a noninvasive supportive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer in cervical scraping specimens.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy; however, early detection remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms and the absence of validated noninvasive triage testing. Diagnosis relies on invasive procedures such as endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage. The EdenDx assay detects hypermethylation of CDO1 and CELF4 genes, which are specifically associated with EC and have been shown to be epigenetically altered prior to symptom onset. Here, we evaluate the clinical and analytical performance of the EdenDx assay as a noninvasive triage tool for the early detect
papers.summary: This study validates the EdenDx assay, which detects hypermethylation of the CDO1 and CELF4 genes in cervical scraping specimens, as a noninvasive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer. The assay aims to reduce reliance on invasive endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage by identifying epigenetic changes that occur before symptom onset. The work reports analytical and clinical performance metrics supporting its use as a supportive triage test.

papers.title: A Guide to Enzymatic Targeted Methylation Sequencing Bioinformatics Workflow: Best Practices.
papers.abstract: We present a best-practices protocol for targeted DNA methylation sequencing analysis that integrates both bisulfite- and enzymatic-conversion approaches using Twist Bioscience technology. Building on established tools and vendor-recommended workflows, this protocol provides a standardized, fully reproducible framework that addresses current gaps in the implementation, documentation, and downstream integration of targeted methylation sequencing analyses. The workflow incorporates widely used open-source tools across two main stages: preprocessing (adapter trimming with Trim Galore and quality
papers.summary: This protocol provides a standardized, reproducible bioinformatics workflow for analyzing targeted DNA methylation sequencing data generated with Twist Bioscience technology, covering both bisulfite- and enzymatic-conversion approaches. It integrates widely used open-source tools across preprocessing (e.g., adapter trimming with Trim Galore) and downstream analysis stages, addressing gaps in implementation, documentation, and integration. The guide aims to help researchers consistently process and interpret targeted methylation data.

papers.title: Epigenetics in cancer: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Epigenetics encompasses heritable yet reversible changes in gene expression that occur without alterations to the underlying DNA sequence. Through coordinated regulation of DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization, epigenetic mechanisms shape chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs that govern cellular identity, plasticity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, disruption of the epigenetic landscape has emerged as a hallmark of tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Unlike gen
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how epigenetic mechanisms—DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization—are disrupted in cancer and contribute to tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. It frames these disruptions as a cancer hallmark and discusses how the reversible nature of epigenetic changes can be leveraged for precision medicine approaches.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses predicted epigenomic features from the pretrained Sei model to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predictions with CTCF ChIP-seq data, it groups binding sites into distinct functional classes, offering insight into how CTCF achieves context-dependent roles in genome organization and gene regulation.

papers.title: Establishment of Uveal Melanoma Patient-Derived Organoids Using an Air-Liquid Interface System for Translational Research.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, with a unique genetic and epigenetic profile and a high metastatic risk. The lack of experimental models to replicate tumor biology, including its epigenetic landscape, limits progress in translational research. Recently, patient-derived organoid (PDO) models have emerged as a promising tool for the modeling of various tumors, including UM. This study aims to establish an air-liquid interface (ALI) PDO culture system for UM, evaluate its similarity to the primary tumors, and assess its utility for drug screening.
papers.summary: This study establishes patient-derived organoids for uveal melanoma using an air-liquid interface culture system, aiming to better replicate the tumor's biology including its epigenetic landscape. The authors evaluate how closely these organoids resemble the original tumors and test their usefulness for drug screening. This provides a new experimental model for a cancer that has lacked representative in vitro systems.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: ChromAgeNet is a convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging from 3D chromatin images. The model learns spatial chromatin features that change with age, offering an interpretable quantitative marker of aging. This demonstrates that chromatin architecture encodes rich aging signatures that can be captured by deep learning.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study examines allele-specific expression in citrus interspecific hybrids, integrating gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNA data to understand how the two subgenomes' distinct epigenetic landscapes interact. The authors report an association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation (via the RdDM pathway) and high expression of certain alleles in citrus genomes, suggesting that methylation in this context can be linked to elevated rather than repressed expression. The work highlights how hybrid epigenomes generate unique expression profiles through the interplay of small RNAs and subgenome-specific methylation patterns.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1 patient variant R5179H, corresp
papers.summary: The authors used CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying the R5179H missense variant in KMT2D, a patient-derived mutation that causes Kabuki syndrome type 1. This complements existing loss-of-function models by allowing study of the 15-30% of patients with missense variants, testing whether they produce comparable phenotypes and may respond to similar postnatal therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context influences regulatory programs in tumors. It argues that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology, they lose spatial information, and spatial methods can reveal tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-cell communication in their native context.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: The authors present a framework for systematically mapping and comparing bacterial DNA methylomes at population scale, prioritizing methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved across taxa. This addresses the current gap in bacterial epigenomics, where methylome maps remain scarce compared to eukaryotes, and enables comparative analysis of epigenetic variation across bacterial populations.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review surveys single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing technologies, computational analysis methods, and applications in precision oncology. It argues that scDNAme overcomes the averaging effect of bulk methylome sequencing, enabling detection of rare epigenetic subclones that drive tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Epigenetics and In Silico Transcriptome Analysis of Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy that accounts for about 15%-20% of childhood leukemias. Despite therapeutic advances, relapses remain common, and survival for high-risk patients is below 60%. Unlike adult AML, pediatric AML displays distinct genetic mutations, including FLT3-ITD, NPM1, KMT2A rearrangements, and core-binding factors (CBF) fusions, as well as extensive epigenetic dysregulation. Aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and altered non-coding RNA expressions disrupt hematopoietic differentiation and activate oncogenic transc
papers.summary: This review examines the epigenetic dysregulation and in silico transcriptome analysis underlying pediatric acute myeloid leukemia, highlighting how aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA expression disrupt hematopoietic differentiation and drive oncogenesis. It emphasizes the distinct genetic landscape of pediatric AML—including FLT3-ITD, NPM1 mutations, KMT2A rearrangements, and CBF fusions—compared to adult disease, and discusses how computational transcriptome approaches can inform understanding of these epigenetic mechanisms.

papers.title: Pan-cancer prognostic value of TGFBR1: Bioinformatics and experimental validation with a focus on gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: TGF-β receptor 1 (TGFBR1) is a key component of TGF-β signaling and has been implicated in tumor progression. However, its expression patterns, prognostic relevance and associated molecular contexts vary among malignancies and remain incompletely characterized within a consistent pan-cancer framework. In the present study, TGFBR1 expression, clinicopathological associations, survival outcomes, immune and stromal infiltration, genomic features, co-expression profiles and transcriptional programs were systematically evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), TCGA-Genotype-Tissue Expression
papers.summary: This study systematically analyzed TGFBR1 expression across multiple cancer types using TCGA data, finding that its prognostic relevance and association with immune/stromal infiltration vary by malignancy. The authors focused on gastric cancer, where they performed experimental validation of TGFBR1's role in tumor progression. The work provides a pan-cancer framework for understanding TGFBR1 as a context-dependent prognostic marker.

papers.title: Targeting the DNHD1‑HDAC6 axis inactivates prostate cancer cell aggressiveness in vitro, suggesting potential therapeutic vulnerability.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer progression toward an aggressive, therapy‑resistant disease state remains a major clinical challenge, indicating a need to identify novel molecular drivers of such progression and actionable therapeutic targets. The present study analyzed the role of dynein heavy chain domain 1 (DNHD1), a previously uncharacterized regulator of malignancy, in prostate cancer. Integrative transcriptomic analyses across The Cancer Genome Atlas and independent clinical cohorts revealed that DNHD1 is markedly upregulated in advanced‑stage prostate cancer and positively correlated with increasing Gl
papers.summary: This study identifies DNHD1 as a novel driver of aggressive prostate cancer, showing it is upregulated in advanced disease and correlates with disease progression. The authors demonstrate that DNHD1 acts through HDAC6, and targeting this axis reduces cancer cell aggressiveness in vitro, suggesting a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation patterns in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS), a form of MS with a short interval between environmental exposure and disease onset. The authors identified differentially methylated regions that link Epstein-Barr virus infection with host immune network genes, suggesting epigenetic mechanisms mediate how EBV exposure contributes to early MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: Data-Driven Virus Discovery with Virushunter and Virusgatherer.
papers.abstract: We present Virushunter and Virusgatherer, a bipartite computational workflow for discovering viral genomes from unprocessed next-generation sequencing data. Virushunter conducts a profile Hidden Markov Model-based sequence homology search for viral hallmark protein-coding sequence reads to construct microcontigs, which are used as seeds for targeted viral genome assembly by Virusgatherer. We showcase the application of Virushunter and Virusgatherer through an RNA virus-wide screen in 3348 bat transcriptome sequencing experiments from the Sequence Read Archive. Many of the discovered viruses ar
papers.summary: The authors present Virushunter and Virusgatherer, a two-part computational pipeline that identifies viral genomes directly from raw next-generation sequencing data. Virushunter uses profile Hidden Markov Models to find viral hallmark protein-coding reads and assemble them into microcontigs, which Virusgatherer then uses as seeds for targeted genome assembly. They demonstrate the workflow by screening 3,348 bat transcriptome experiments from the Sequence Read Archive, uncovering many previously unknown RNA viruses.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four disti
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline to map partially methylated domains (PMDs) across cancers and applied it to esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, classifying PMDs into four distinct subtypes based on gene expression patterns. These PMD subtypes show different epigenetic features and appear to regulate epithelial-mesenchymal transition and immune suppression, linking widespread hypomethylation to tumor progression.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variation in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or distorted accessibility signals. The authors show that incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as an input control, analogous to ChIP-seq input controls, corrects for these DNA dosage biases and yields more and wider ATAC peaks that better reflect true regulatory regions. This provides a simple methodological improvement for chromatin accessibility studies.

papers.title: Characteristics of predicated pathogenic missense variants in human genes for Mendelian disorders.
papers.abstract: Missense variants represent a major class of genetic variation and contribute substantially to the cause of Mendelian disorders. However, the genetic and protein properties governing their pathogenicity remain incompletely characterized. Existing variant pathogenicity databases, such as ClinVar, are enriched for variants in well-studied genes and therefore may not provide a representative view of pathogenic missense variants across the genome. Meanwhile, recent advances in computational pathogenicity prediction have significantly improved their predictive accuracy, enabling large-scale genome-
papers.summary: This study characterizes the genetic and protein properties that distinguish predicted pathogenic missense variants from benign ones across human genes linked to Mendelian disorders. Using computational pathogenicity predictions rather than relying on ClinVar, which is biased toward well-studied genes, the authors provide a more genome-wide view of what makes missense variants pathogenic. The work helps clarify features like conservation, protein domain location, and amino acid changes that drive pathogenicity.

papers.title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL implicating actin remodeling in COVID-19 severity in a Pakistani cohort.
papers.abstract: The current study investigated host genetic associations with disease severity in COVID-19 patients of South Asian origin and explored its molecular basis.
papers.summary: This study performed whole-exome sequencing on a Pakistani cohort to identify host genetic variants associated with COVID-19 severity, finding a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL. The finding implicates actin remodeling pathways in COVID-19 pathogenesis and highlights the value of studying diverse populations for host genetics of infectious disease.

papers.title: VarSim: A Python Toolkit for HGVS Variant Description Validation, Normalization, and Representation Conversion.
papers.abstract: Accurate and reproducible representation of genetic variants is essential for clinical genomics, variant databases, and genomic research. The Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) recommendations provide a standardized framework for describing sequence variants, but practical HGVS processing commonly involves multiple interdependent tasks, including parsing, validation, normalization, coordinate transformation, protein consequence inference, and conversion between variant representation formats. We developed VarSim, a lightweight Python toolkit that integrates these operations within a referen
papers.summary: VarSim is a lightweight Python toolkit that integrates HGVS variant parsing, validation, normalization, coordinate transformation, protein consequence inference, and format conversion into a single reference-based workflow. It addresses the common need in clinical genomics and variant databases for accurate, reproducible variant representation by unifying multiple interdependent HGVS processing tasks.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for precision gene therapy: emerging technologies, clinical applications, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing gene therapy from an empirical and iterative process to a predictive, data-driven and increasingly intelligent therapeutic development approach. This review covers the application of AI extensively throughout the gene therapy development process, from target therapeutic discovery, identification of disease genes, variant interpretation, integration of multi-omics data, optimization of CRISPR, engineering of the vector, prediction of immunogenicity, manufacturing, and clinical development and post-marketing surveillance. The role of machine learni
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the gene therapy development pipeline, from disease gene identification and variant interpretation through CRISPR optimization, vector engineering, immunogenicity prediction, manufacturing, and post-marketing surveillance. It argues that AI is shifting gene therapy from empirical iteration toward predictive, data-driven therapeutic development, and outlines emerging technologies, clinical applications, and future directions.

papers.title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Zamia integrifolia uncovers distinct patterns of genomic turnover and repeat expansion in Zamiaceae.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperm mitochondrial genomes exhibit substantial variation in size and structure, yet the evolutionary dynamics of Cycadales remain insufficiently explored beyond the genus Cycas.
papers.summary: This study reports the complete mitochondrial genome of Zamia integrifolia, the first from a cycad genus other than Cycas, revealing substantial genomic turnover and repeat expansion within Zamiaceae. The findings highlight distinct evolutionary dynamics in cycad mitochondrial genomes, expanding understanding beyond the previously studied Cycas genus.

papers.title: Precision engineering of upstream open reading frames for translational regulation and crop improvement.
papers.abstract: Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are pervasive cis-regulatory elements in the 5'untranslated regions (UTRs) of eukaryotic mRNAs that modulate translation of downstream main open reading frames (mORFs) by shaping ribosome scanning, initiation, and reinitiation. By operating downstream of transcription, uORFs enable fine-scale control of protein abundance, offering a distinctive regulatory layer for precise tuning of gene expression in plants. Recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, peptidomics, computational annotation, and genome editing have expanded th
papers.summary: This review discusses how upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in 5' untranslated regions act as cis-regulatory elements that fine-tune translation of downstream main ORFs by influencing ribosome scanning, initiation, and reinitiation. It highlights recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, peptidomics, computational annotation, and genome editing that enable precise engineering of uORFs for translational control. The authors argue that uORF engineering offers a distinctive post-transcriptional layer for tuning gene expression in plants, with applications for crop improvement.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for interpreting phylogenetic tree patterns in interkingdom horizontal gene transfer.
papers.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT), the movement of genetic material between unrelated organisms, is widely recognized as an important driver of genome evolution in bacteria. In eukaryotes, however, the evolutionary impact of HGT remains debated. The identification of interkingdom HGT (iHGT) is especially challenging due to the lack of gold standard methods. While automated approaches for iHGT candidate detection exist, the interpretation of phylogenetic tree topologies into biologically meaningful evolutionary patterns has traditionally depended on expert manual inspection, a process that is subj
papers.summary: The authors present a machine learning framework designed to automatically interpret phylogenetic tree topologies in the context of interkingdom horizontal gene transfer, replacing the traditional reliance on expert manual inspection. This addresses a key bottleneck in iHGT detection, where candidate identification is automated but biological interpretation of tree patterns remains labor-intensive and subjective. The work aims to make large-scale iHGT analysis more scalable and reproducible.

papers.title: ChoCallate: a computational pipeline for consensus germline variant calling in genomic sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Accurate germline variant calling in non-model and polyploid organisms remains challenging due to sequencing errors, genomic complexity, and caller-specific biases. Existing ensemble methods of variant calling are constrained by species-specific training, limited portability, or an inability to process multiple samples concurrently. To address these limitations we developed ChoCallate, a Nextflow-based pipeline for consensus germline variant calling. The pipeline integrates three species-independent callers, bcftools, FreeBayes, and Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) HaplotypeCaller, within a flex
papers.summary: ChoCallate is a Nextflow-based pipeline that combines three species-independent variant callers (bcftools, FreeBayes, and GATK HaplotypeCaller) to produce consensus germline variant calls. It is designed to handle non-model and polyploid organisms and can process multiple samples concurrently, addressing limitations of existing ensemble methods that require species-specific training or lack scalability.

papers.title: Novel Strategy for Structural Variant Genotyping by Short-Read Genomic Sequencing From Restriction-Circles: Experimental and Bioinformatics Proof-of-Concept.
papers.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) comprise copy-number variants (e.g., deletions and duplications) and copy-neutral SV (e.g., perfect inversions). Short-read high-throughput DNA-sequencing is the established technology for small-variant calling in clinical genomics, whereas Oxford nanopore or PacBio long-read NGS technologies improve SV identification but remain challenging to implement in clinical settings. We developed and validated a novel experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline for SV genotyping from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of restriction-circles of DNA. The experimental
papers.summary: The authors present a new experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline for genotyping structural variants (including copy-number changes and perfect inversions) using short-read whole-genome sequencing of DNA that has been circularized by restriction enzymes (restriction-circles). This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that short-read sequencing, which is already established in clinical genomics, can be adapted to detect structural variants that typically require long-read technologies. The approach could make SV genotyping more accessible in clinical settings without the need for Oxford Nanopore or PacBio platforms.
